newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Up on bids, fewer Mideast supplies.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Up on bids, fewer Mideast supplies.

text.p: Singapore high sulphur fuel oil prices firmed amid strong bids from local traders and reduced Mideast supplies arriving in Asia, traders said on Wednesday.
By market close, a 20,000 tonne cargo of 180-cst supplies for loading July 24-August 1 was sold by a European major to a local trader at $97.50 per tonne, fob.
The same local trader purchased three 20,000 tonne cargoes for July 16-20 loading on Tuesday at $96.50-$97.50.
Traders said prices have firmed with the fresh bids that have been absent in the past week.
They said prices were further supported by reduced Mideast supplies coming to Asia.
They said strong Mideast demand has absorbed supplies and have limited any surplus cargoes from flowing to this region.
Thailand has awarded its tender to buy 80,000 tonnes of fuel oil for August 15-25 delivery to Sri Racha at $8.50 per tonne premium over Singapore spot quotes.
The tender sought 75,000 tonnes of 180-cst grade, 2.0-percent sulphur and 5,000 tonnes of 180-cst, 1.0-percent fuel oil.
Thin bunker trading gave little support to prices, traders said.

Major oil firms said they would rather dispose of their fuel oil supplies in the cargo market, citing poor bunker sales and dimishing profits as spread between cargo and bunker prices narrow to as low as $2-$3 per tonne.
Swaps were also quoted higher, with July at $98.50/$99.25 and August at $98.50/$99.25, 25 cents firmer from Tuesday quotes.
